B: Middle sub-image labeled Right forearm shows purpuric papules consistent with described DGI skin exam in same patient. C: Right sub-image labeled Right foot shows scattered purpuric papules consistent with described DGI skin exam in same patient.

in_text_mentions: d right ankle, and had prominent metacarpophalangeal joint pain with passive flexion and extension of his fingers, indicating tenosynovitis. Skin exam showed multiple small purpuric stellate papules and patches with mildly erythematous borders on his upper and lower extremities (Figure 3). His CRP was elevated to 400 milligrams/liter and his troponin peaked at 19 nanograms/milliliter. He refused myocardial biopsy. However, a skin biopsy revealed extensive intravascular fibrin thrombi with secondary epidermal changes; Gram and Steiner stains showed rare diplococci within the vessels (Figure 4).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is a patient MRI of right hand in a case report titled Disseminated Gonococcal Infection Presenting as Isolated Septic Arthritis, caption describes synovial enhancement/effusion/periarticular edema of third MCP concerning for septic arthritis, matching synovitis with effusion MRI manifestation of DGI. B: Panel B is patient MRI proton density with contrast showing synovial hyperenhancement of third MCP joint in DGI presenting as septic arthritis, matching enhancing synovitis manifestation. C: Panel C is patient MRI T1 post-contrast showing effusion with synovial enhancement and periarticular edema of third MCP joint in DGI septic arthritis case, matching synovitis with effusion MRI manifestation.

panels.figure_caption: MRI of the right hand showing T1-weighted sagittal (A), proton density with contrast (B), and T1-weighted post-contrast (C) views showing synovial enhancement, effusion, and periarticular edema surrounding the third right MCP joint. (A) Joint capsule hyperenhancement is indicated by the white arrow, and subcutaneous hyperenhancement is indicated by the red arrow. (B) Synovial hyperenhancement is highlighted by the white arrow. (C) Effusion is shown by the white arrow. MRI: magnetic resonance imaging; MCP: metacarpophalangeal
in_text_mentions: DNA, and a respiratory viral panel were negative. A bilateral hand X-ray revealed no acute osseous abnormalities. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the right hand revealed a large third MCP joint effusion with synovial enhancement and marked surrounding periarticular edema, concerning for septic arthritis (Figure 2). Orthopedic surgery was consulted and recommended one dose of intravenous (IV) vancomycin for empiric coverage of the septic joint and took the patient to the operating room on the day of admission for arthrotomy with debridement and irrigation (D&I) of the right third MCP joint.

Caption states 'red papules on his trunk and extremities (A and B)' as 'Skin manifestations of disseminated gonococcal infection' in article titled disseminated gonococcal infection. Caption states 'red papules on his trunk and extremities (A and B)' as skin manifestations of disseminated gonococcal infection. Caption and in-text describe 'impetigo-like pustular lesion' / 'pustular lesion' as skin manifestation of disseminated gonococcal infection, matching sparse acral pustular lesions.
